command: cargo run -p pool-sim --release --example ladder -- --curves data/curves --out data/fitting/ladder-results.json
notes: every cushion number here runs on the core with `solve_wall`'s rounding window made two-sided: the one-sided reading (`d0 <= slop`) treated any ball behind a wall face's plane as touching it, and a jaw face's plane runs across the table's interior, so a ball rebounding off a long rail beside a side mouth took a spurious jaw impulse. Before the fix the rolling square-hit retention measured 0.6374 at e_n 0.78 (spec 0.6992); after it, 0.6992.

no corpus or spec number was edited to make a stage pass; where a produced value differs from `physics.md` §6's stated number, the check's note names the mechanism and the gate is left as the spec states it.
spec: docs/spec/physics.md §6 (the fitting ladder, stages 1–4, amended at #8)

checks.label: gate
checks.name: pure-spin branch vs TP B-8
checks.note: the relation is exact for the cloth model; the gate is the spec's recorded instance as a ceiling

checks.label: measured
checks.name: TP B-5 rolling direct-hit ratio — draw-follow file block (e_b 1.0, mu_b 0.06)
checks.note: the file's ratio is derived (mu_b 0.06, e_b 0.94) and speed-independent; the model's is neither

checks.label: measured
checks.name: TP B-5 rolling direct-hit ratio — TP B-5 constants (e_b 0.94, mu_b 0.06)
checks.note: the file's ratio is derived (mu_b 0.06, e_b 0.94) and speed-independent; the model's is neither

checks.label: measured
checks.name: TP B-5 rolling direct-hit ratio — shipped default profile (e_b 0.95, mu_b table)
checks.note: the file's ratio is derived (mu_b 0.06, e_b 0.94) and speed-independent; the model's is neither

checks.label: gate
checks.name: TP B-5 rolling direct-hit ratio
checks.note: the gate is the spec's recorded instance within the curves' own 2 % band

checks.label: residual
checks.name: TP B-8 full-row comparison (in-domain rows)
checks.note: reported, not gated: the relation is a free-space spin-only upper bound and 85 of the 120 digitized rows sit outside its domain
checks.spec: ~50 % mean error, structural (−26 % spin damping + ~2.5 % forward residual)

stages.method: TP B-8's free-space closed form d = 2R²/(49g)(1/μs + 1/μr)ω² for the pure-spin branch; TP B-5's rolling direct hit as a 600 mm pair in free space, the cue ball launched rolling at the file's speed with the pre-impact roll loss corrected; TP B-8's 120 survey rows with the cue ball launched at the row's pre-impact speed and spin, the object ball its `drag` ahead
stages.name: long straight stop / draw / follow
notes: the B-5 rows beyond the prototype's three speeds are detail only: a free-space ball still lands somewhere, and past ~12 mph the ball-ball contact's vertical impulse carries the object ball's landing outside the 2.54 m × 1.27 m bounds, where the model ends it as off-table — the ratio is meaningless there, and the gate runs the three speeds the spec's instance ran
stages.verdict: pure-spin max rel err 0.0000 % (spec 0.012 %); B-5 ratio 7.781 at the draw-follow block (spec 7.781, file 7.559); full-row comparison reported (35 in-domain rows, mean |err| 462.2 mm / 51.2 %)

checks.label: gate
checks.name: throw sign convention (§3.2)
checks.note: the object ball departs toward the cue ball's incoming line, away from the tangent line
checks.spec: a no-english cut gives a negative throw_deg

checks.label: residual
checks.name: the shipped μb table's six-point residual
checks.note: the structural offset the stick/slip re-pin is expected to remove — reported, not the gate

checks.label: gate
checks.name: μb refit residual
checks.note: the gate is only the refit, and a lower residual passes it; the shipped table's residual is the expected offset (§6)

stages.method: TP B-3's six measured points, compared as |throw_deg| (§3.2's sign convention is checked on the produced values); each shot is a free-space cut with the impact parameter b = 2R sin φ, the cue ball arriving at the row's speed (stun, no english) through the declaration path's own tip offsets; μb refitted by multi-start pattern search over the mean |err|
stages.name: cuts at known angles
notes: the refit's landscape is flat enough that the coefficients are not the observable: the search lands on a/b/c = 0.0361/0.2398/0.975 (mu_b(1 m/s) = 0.1266) with a residual below the spec's 0.908°, while the spec's own refit (0.0010/0.2732/0.620, mu_b(1 m/s) = 0.148) is also a solution — the six-point residual is what the gate reads, and both sit far outside the provisional 0.03–0.08 band (§3.2's not-portable marking)
stages.observable: throw vs cut angle and speed
stages.verdict: refit residual 0.742° (gate 0.908°, spec's refit a/b/c = 0.0010/0.2732/0.620); produced fit a/b/c = 0.0361/0.2398/0.975; shipped-table residual 3.562° (spec 4.167°)

checks.label: gate
checks.name: single square-hit retention
checks.note: TP B-6's measured e_c = 0.70 ± the source's scatter; the spec's e_n fit is 0.75 → 0.6714, 0.80 → 0.7178

checks.label: derived
checks.name: the e_n that reproduces the measured retention
checks.note: the default's provenance: TP B-6's measured retention e_c = 0.70 (§3.3/§5)

checks.label: gate
checks.name: e_n fit inside the measured range
checks.note: the bisected e_n lands on the default's neighbourhood

checks.label: derived
checks.name: horizontal COR from the normal channel alone
checks.note: the whole retention share above this is the tangential and vertical channels (§3.3)

checks.label: residual
checks.name: TP B-6 travel anchors
checks.note: reported, not gated: the shortfall is structural — e_n trades retention for travel and μc is flat under the ruled 3D channel; the spec's instance concentrates it at the three slow anchors

stages.method: The retention probe is the spec's pinned one — the table reduced to its four rails, a stun ball square into the long cushion's flat face from the x = −300 mm lane, the speeds sampled either side of the contact — with a natural-roll variant reported beside it; the travel anchors run the head spot's rolling ball into the short rails with the path length sampled from the exact timeline; e_n is fitted by bisection on the mean retention
stages.name: cushion retention and rail travel
notes: the WPA 4–4.5-table-length acceptance test is dropped by the amended gate and is not implemented: at the measured coefficients it needs ≈9 m/s

the retention gate runs the natural roll probe: the spec's 0.6714 / 0.6992 / 0.7178 are a rolling ball's, and a stun ball is still skidding when it reaches the cushion at the fast end (its slide-to-roll distance grows as v², 262 mm at 1.5 m/s but 1.05 m at 3 m/s), which is what drags the stun probe's mean down

rows.probe: stun declaration, still skidding at the fast end

stages.verdict: retention 0.6992 at e_n 0.78 with the natural roll probe (measured 0.70 ± 0.02); fitted e_n 0.7808 (spec 0.78); travel anchors mean |err| 0.339 lengths (spec 0.337, reported not gated)

checks.label: derived
checks.name: reference tip offset implied by tan α = a/L
checks.note: the only offset at which Platinum's 46 shafts are self-consistent (§3.6)

checks.label: gate
checks.name: squirt band at the reference tip offset
checks.note: the model's band at the pinned offset reproduces the spec's instance; the published bands do not agree with each other (Shepard 0.5–2.3 vs Platinum 1.3–2.3)

checks.label: gate
checks.name: squirt band's upper end
checks.note: the short-pivot bookend, where the model sits above Platinum's quoted 2.3°

checks.label: derived
checks.name: the void 0.5 R comparison
checks.note: reported so it is not re-attempted: 0.5 R offsets put the model above every published band

stages.method: Platinum's 46-shaft table: the reference tip offset implied by tan α = a/L per shaft, then the model's squirt angle at that offset through the declaration path (aim +x, `spin[0]` = a/ρ_max, `sin α = a/√(a² + L²)`), evaluated at the pivot bookends
stages.name: pivot-length test per cue
notes: the table's own angle column runs 1.3352–2.3131°, so the produced band (1.29–2.39) is the pinned offset's algebra, not the source's own column
stages.verdict: band 1.29–2.39° at a = 8.07 mm (0.282 R, sd 0.10 mm); spec 1.29–2.39°, Platinum published 1.3–2.3°, the 0.5 R comparison void at 4.23°
